meta.title: Digital-health platforms and equity in avoidable admissions

primary.text: To what extent do regional digital-health platforms reduce avoidable hospital admissions for patients with chronic conditions, and how is that reduction distributed across income groups?
criteria: the reduction in avoidable admissions per 1,000 chronic patients
the ratio of that reduction in the lowest income quintile to the highest
primary.operationalisation: Avoidable admissions are the ambulatory-care-sensitive conditions set, counted per 1,000 registered chronic patients per year; equity is the ratio of the platform effect in the lowest income quintile to the effect in the highest, with the quintile assigned from the patient's exemption category.
primary.scope: Six Italian regions that activated a platform between 2019 and 2023; patients aged 18 and over with at least one chronic condition; 2016 to 2026.
primary.completion_criterion: The question is answered when a region-level effect on avoidable admissions is estimated against non-adopting regions and the equity ratio is reported with its confidence interval.

method.approach: Staggered difference-in-differences on administrative hospital records, with event-study checks and a synthetic control for the earliest adopter.
sources: Hospital discharge records, 2016-2026, Ministry of Health
Chronic-disease exemption registry, 2016-2026, regional health agencies
Platform activation dates and covered services, 2019-2023, regional health agencies
method.procedure: Define the six treated regions and the eligible control regions; aggregate discharges to region-year cells by condition set and income quintile; estimate the effect of activation with region and year fixed effects; inspect event-study leads for pre-trends; repeat the estimate for each quintile and report the ratio; run a synthetic control for the 2019 adopter as a robustness check.
validity_conditions: Regions are compared before and after activation, with non-adopting regions as controls
Discharge coding stays stable across the period, checked on a fixed set of diagnoses
Income quintile is observed for every patient through the exemption category
limits: The design estimates the effect of activation, not of platform use intensity
Regions that activated before 2019 fall outside the comparison
Avoidable admissions measure access, not the clinical quality of ambulatory care
The equity ratio is sensitive to how patients without an exemption are assigned

results.claim: Activation reduces avoidable admissions by between 3 and 6 per cent, and the reduction is smaller in the lowest income quintile than in the highest.
results.falsifier: The estimated effect on avoidable admissions is indistinguishable from zero in every treated region, or the lowest quintile shows a reduction at least as large as the highest in all regions.
results.evidence_needed: Region-year discharge counts by condition set and quintile for the full period, plus activation dates for all six regions.

results.claim: An open dataset of region-level avoidable-admission rates by condition set and income quintile, 2016-2026, with the code that builds it.
results.evidence_needed: The published dataset and its build script, deposited with the project's data package.

warrant.gap_statement: Evaluations of Italian digital-health platforms stop at single-region case studies and do not test whether the recorded reduction reaches low-income patients.
evidence: Ministry of Health, hospital discharge records, 2024 release
MUR, PRIN 2026 evaluation guidelines, D.D. 2298 All. 3
OECD, Health at a Glance: Europe, 2024

normative_premises: Equal access to care for equal need is a condition of a legitimate regional health service
A reduction in admissions that accrues only to the better-off does not count as an improvement
criteria: the absolute reduction in avoidable admissions
the ratio between the lowest and the highest income quintile
